source.rows: Strategies #50-#85 KEEP (incl. #57 filters, #58, #55 exit), I1-I5, P1 (P1a-P1f), P2-P16

conventions: signal-bar close then next-bar open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; non-alternating swings, 5-bar fractal = strength 2; el_* comparisons; ATR is WFSafe_AvgTrueRange

candidates.name: SwingPivotSequence
candidates.quote: 5-bar fractals ordered low, high, low, high.
candidates.description: The merged, newest-first list of the most recent confirmed swing pivots of strength S (non-alternating EL SwingHigh/SwingLow semantics) inside a lookback window: each entry carries its type (+1 high, -1 low), its price and its bars-ago. Shared by every fractal-ORDER rule in this file (#50, #51, #53, #59, P6). Rules that only need one side (#52, #58, P9, P13, P15, I2-I4) read the per-side occurrences of the measured port directly.

complexity.reason: swing-pivot detection on both series merged into one ordered sequence

library_check.origin: Brooks corpus (pivot primitive, measured with EL_Swing_Probe)
library_check.evidence: SwingHigh/SwingLow give per-side occurrences only; HigherSwingLow and ThreePushPattern inline the same scan per side. No rule merges both sides into one ordered sequence, which is what 'fractal order' needs.

notes: 5-bar fractal = strength 2 (MINING convention); strength is the input.
The EL twin can rebuild the sequence from SwingHighBar/SwingLowBar occurrences (bar indices, so guarded on <> -1, never on price).
A bar that is both a swing high and a swing low (an outside-bar pivot) enters the list twice at the same bars-ago; their relative order is an open question.

candidates.name: FractalBoxBreakout
candidates.quote: 5-bar fractals ordered low, high, low, high. The last two are within the range of the first two. Enter on the first candle to close outside the range of the last two. If it closes above, enter long.
candidates.description: The four most recent pivots, oldest to newest, are low L1, high H1, low L2, high H2 with L2 and H2 both inside [L1, H1] (a contracting box). Long on the first close above H2 since H2 printed; short on the first close below L2. p.60 (the fade) is the same rule with the per-placement flip.
candidates.sides: mirrored trigger only: the pivot pattern (L,H,L,H) is the same on both sides, the short fires on the close below L2

complexity.reason: ordered pivot pattern over a variable-length window plus a first-close-outside test

library_check.evidence: Closest: DoubleExtremeBreakout and TrendLineBreak (Brooks) break a level built from two same-side pivots; nothing tests an L-H-L-H contraction box.

notes: 'Within the range of the first two' read inclusively (el_ge/el_le).
The rule fires only while these four are still the four most recent pivots; a newer pivot inside the box replaces the pattern.
Whether the mirrored ordering H,L,H,L should also qualify is an open question (the note states only L,H,L,H).

candidates.name: LateFractalFade
candidates.quote: Calculate average number of bars between fractal points over the last 8+ fractals. Next fractal comes 2-3x the average number of bars later. If it is a fractal high, enter short. If it is a fractal low, enter long.
candidates.description: On the bar a new pivot is confirmed, compare the gap since the previous pivot (either type) with the mean gap between the F pivots before it. If the new gap is at least K times the mean, fade the pivot: a late swing low is a long, a late swing high a short.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (enter on the confirmation bar's close, next open)

complexity.reason: pivot sequence plus inter-pivot timing statistics

library_check.evidence: No rule in the catalog measures the timing between pivots; SwingLegLengthAtLeast tests a fixed minimum leg length in bars, not relative lateness.

notes: '2-3x' is read as a minimum multiple (default 2, range 2-3); an upper cap was not stated.
The signal is confirmed `strength` bars after the pivot bar, by construction.
lookback must hold pivotCount + 1 pivots; 300 bars is a starting point.

candidates.name: FractalTrendlineBreak
candidates.quote: Downward trendline defined by 3 or more consecutive fractal highs (5-bar) for which linear regression gives R^2 < Y. Enter long on first candle to close above the trendline. Invalidate trendline if it happened more than Z bars ago or if there is a close that crosses it.
candidates.description: Least-squares line through the M most recent swing highs (price on bar index). It qualifies when R^2 > Y (Brian's correction), its slope is at most -minSlope ATR per bar, and its newest pivot is no more than Z bars old. Long on the first close above the projected line, no close having crossed it since the newest pivot. Short mirrors on an up-line through swing lows; p.63's fade is the flip toggle.

complexity.reason: pivot detection, least-squares fit with R^2, and line projection

library_check.evidence: TrendLineBreak draws a two-pivot line through the two most recent swing highs and fires on the close through it; this fits M >= 3 pivots by regression and gates on R^2, slope and age. At M = 2 R^2 is identically 1 and the line is TrendLineBreak's, so the two coincide only at that degenerate setting (minus the slope and age gates).

notes: The raw note says R^2 < Y; TRIAGE (Brian 2026-11-05) corrects it to R^2 > Y.
Sums are centred on the means so the fit is shift-invariant in floating point too; the EL twin must sum in the same order (newest-first).
slopeAgo >= minSlope*ATR means the line FALLS going forward (bars-ago axis); minSlope and Z defaults are not in the note.

candidates.name: FractalOrderLowHighHigh
candidates.quote: Order of fractals is low, high, high. Enter long. Order of fractals is high, low, low. Enter short.
candidates.description: The three most recent pivots, oldest to newest, are a swing low followed by two swing highs (no low between them, possible because swings are non-alternating): long. High, low, low: short. Fires on the bar the third pivot is confirmed.

library_check.evidence: HigherSwingLow / ThreePushPattern compare pivot PRICES on one side; nothing reads the TYPE order of the merged sequence. No price relation between the two highs is required here.

notes: Fired as an event (the confirmation bar). Holding it as a state until the next pivot is the other reading; see open_questions.

candidates.name: MomentumLadder
candidates.quote: Close > Close [X] > Close [2X] > Close [4X] Enter long
candidates.description: Closes sampled at 0, X, 2X and 4X bars ago are strictly descending into the past: a ladder of momentum on three horizons. Long; .2 (short on the same condition) is the flip.
candidates.pseudocode: long = el_gt(close[0], close[X]) && el_gt(close[X], close[2 * X]) && el_gt(close[2 * X], close[4 * X]);

library_check.origin: original corpus ported from StrategyGeneratorTS (Davey-style momentum, per TRIAGE #60)
library_check.evidence: Momentum(X) is the first link only; the later links compare LAGGED closes with each other, which no Momentum placement (always anchored at close[0]) reaches. ClosingPatternOne (EEC) orders closes at 1-3 bars, not a scaled ladder.

notes: X default is not in the note; 20 with a 5-50 range. Reaches back 4X.
Davey-style momentum is a pane-2 trend filter only (Decision 3); here the ladder shape is the entry, which TRIAGE kept.

candidates.name: AdxFallingMomentumFade
candidates.quote: ADX[1] < ADX[Z] Close[1] > Close[Z] Enter short ... ADX[1] < ADX[Z] Close[1] < Close[Z] Enter long
candidates.description: A divergence between trend strength and price: ADX has fallen from Z bars ago to the last bar while price has risen over the same span: short (fade); price fell with ADX falling: long. .4 is the flip. Kept as one candidate because the two halves share Z and only mean something as a pair (the divergence twist Decision 5 keeps).
candidates.pseudocode:
long = el_lt(adx[1], adx[Z]) && el_lt(close[1], close[Z]);
// short: el_lt(adx[1], adx[Z]) && el_gt(close[1], close[Z])
candidates.sides: mirrored (the ADX term is identical on both sides; only the close comparison flips)

complexity.reason: reads ADX's own history, which needs a mirrored series buffer

library_check.evidence: AdxBelowThreshold and EecTwoAmigos threshold the ADX level; no rule compares ADX with its own lagged value. The close half alone is Momentum at lag Z shifted one bar.

notes: Z has no default in the note; 10, range 5-30.
adx[Z] is WFSafe_ADX's function history; the C++ must mirror it in a buffer, zero-filled before the first evaluated bar (CLAUDE.md zero-fill convention).

candidates.name: AdxRisingExit
candidates.quote: Exit if ADX[1] > ADX[Z]
candidates.description: Exit any position once ADX has risen from Z bars ago to the last bar: the trend is strengthening against a fade.
candidates.pseudocode: exitLong = el_gt(adx[1], adx[Z]);   // identical for exitShort

library_check.evidence: No ADX-slope exit; AtrRising is the ATR analogue as an entry filter.

notes: Reads no position state: an exit by placement. Shares Z with ON-55 by default.

candidates.name: AtrShortLongRatio
candidates.quote: Volatility - ATR (compare short to long ATR)
candidates.description: The short-window ATR is at least K times the long-window ATR (volatility expanding); negate for contraction.
candidates.pseudocode: pass = el_ge(atrFast, multiple * atrSlow);   // same both sides

library_check.origin: unknown (AtrFastAboveSlow, Aug 2026 batch); TrueRangeAvgRatio is from the 'AI Book' batch
library_check.evidence: AtrFastAboveSlow is this at multiple = 1 (WFSafe ATRs); TrueRangeAvgRatio carries the multiple K over fresh TR means (lookback, lookback*slowFactor). Any K != 1 with WFSafe ATRs would be AtrFastAboveSlow `extends` (one new input).

notes: Pullback Study filter; Davey's study frame itself is excluded (Decision 3).

candidates.name: TrueRangeCoefficientOfVariation
candidates.quote: Volatility - Coefficient of variation
candidates.description: The coefficient of variation of the true range over N bars (population StdDev / mean) is at most T: volatility is steady. Negate for erratic volatility.
candidates.pseudocode:
m = average(trueRange, N); s = stddev(trueRange, N);   // population form, fresh, newest-first
pass = el_le(s, cvMax * m);   // product form, no divide

library_check.evidence: BarRangeAboveStd uses the same mean/StdDev pair to flag one outsized bar; nothing thresholds the dispersion of the window itself.

notes: CV of CLOSE (the textbook form) is std/mean of price and fails the shift test; true range is substituted. Which series Brian meant is an open question.
Average/StdDev over a price EXPRESSION read real history (fresh loops), not a zero-filled variable.

candidates.name: AdxTrendFilter
candidates.quote: Trend - ADX
candidates.description: ADX(14) below (or, negated, at or above) a threshold.
candidates.pseudocode: pass = el_lt(adx, threshold);

library_check.evidence: Identical test, both sides same; the negate toggle gives the trending reading.

candidates.name: ChoppinessIndexAbove
candidates.quote: Choppiness Index CI = 100 x log10(Sum of ATR (14-day) / Range) / log10(14)
candidates.description: Choppiness Index over N bars above T (choppy). CI > T is equivalent to Range < ATR x N^(1 - T/100), so it is RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple with rangeLookback = atrLookback = N and rangeAtrMultiple = N^(1 - T/100); no logarithm is needed.
candidates.pseudocode:
// CI = 100*log10(N*atr/range)/log10(N) > T  <=>  range < atr * pow(N, 1 - T/100)
pass = el_le(highest(high, N) - lowest(low, N), N_pow * atr(N));  // N_pow precomputed per grid point

library_check.evidence: Monotone transform: choppy CI > T fires on the bars RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple(N, N^(1-T/100), N) fires on (61.8 at N=14 gives K = 14^0.382 = 2.74). Differences: the textbook CI uses Sum(TR(1)) and true high/low; the library uses the WFSafe rolling ATR and plain highs/lows. Same as I5 up to the constant.

notes: log/log10 have no EL_FEATURES row (UNKNOWN); the transform avoids them, and pow can be done in the grid instead of in EL.
The note's 'Sum of ATR (14-day)' is read as the sum of 1-bar true ranges over 14 bars, the standard CI.

candidates.name: StopBeyondRecentFractal
candidates.quote: Stop loss below the most recent fractal high / low
candidates.description: A long exits when the close falls to or below the most recent confirmed swing low (5-bar fractal); a short above the most recent swing high.
candidates.pseudocode: exitLong = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && haveLo1 && el_le(close[0], lo1 - offsetTicks * tick);

library_check.evidence: SwingPointTrailingStop at trailOffsetTicks = 0 (default 1) re-reads the latest pivot every bar. If 'most recent' means the pivot at ENTRY, it is InitialStopBeyondSwingAtEntry (also Brooks) at stopTicks = 0.

notes: Close-based like the library's (the standing convention for stops).

candidates.name: FractalLegSlopeDecay
candidates.quote: Fractal pattern goes low, high, low, high. Slope on the last leg up (low to high) is less than the slope on the first leg up (first low to high). Enter short.
candidates.description: The four most recent pivots are L1, H1, L2, H2 (oldest to newest) and the last up-leg L2->H2 rises more slowly per bar than the first up-leg L1->H1: momentum is fading, short. The long side is the mirror: H, L, H, L with the last down-leg shallower than the first. Fires on the bar H2 (L2 on the long side) is confirmed.

library_check.evidence: ThreePushPattern's converging shapeMode compares push EXTENTS on one side; TrendLineSlopeFlattening compares trend-line slopes. Neither compares the slopes of two legs of an L-H-L-H sequence.

notes: Slopes in price per bar; the ratio test is scale-free and shift-invariant. No price relation (e.g. H2 > H1) is required by the note.

candidates.name: MaStackGapNarrowing
candidates.quote: Upward moving averages have not crossed to the downside but the gap between them is narrower than it was X bars ago.
candidates.description: The note's case is the SHORT side: fast MA above slow MA, both rising over X bars, but the gap fast - slow is smaller than X bars ago (an uptrend losing steam). Long side mirrors: falling stack, fast below slow, gap narrowing.
candidates.sides: mirrored (the note's uptrend case is the short side)

library_check.evidence: ChannelWidthConvergence measures a narrowing between two pivot LINES; EmaSlope tests one EMA's rise. Nothing reads the gap between two MAs against its own past.

notes: MA type and lengths are not in the note: EMAs 20/50 (the corpus's measured WFSafe_Xaverage). 'Upward' read as each MA above its own value X bars ago.
EMA history reads need a mirrored buffer (zero-filled before the first bar).

candidates.name: NewXBarLowEntry
candidates.quote: Candle makes a new X bar low. Enter short.
candidates.description: The bar's low is at or below the lowest low of the last X bars: short (long mirrors on a new X-bar high). The classic trigger paired with ON-61-a's novel filter (Decision 10).
candidates.pseudocode: long = el_ge(high[0], highest(high, X));   // short: el_le(low[0], lowest(low, X))

library_check.evidence: HighestHighBreakout's short side is exactly 'low at or below the lowest low of the last N bars', current bar included; X shared with ON-61-a.

candidates.name: NewExtremeFrequency
candidates.quote: Trend strength indicator: What fraction of the last X bars made a Y bar low?
candidates.description: At least a fraction F of the last X bars each made a Y-bar low (short side: downtrend strength); the long side counts Y-bar highs.

library_check.evidence: HighestHighBreakout tests the current bar only; HigherLowCount counts adjacent-bar higher lows; TrendBarCountDominanceInWindow counts trend bars. Nothing counts new Y-bar extremes in a window.

notes: 'Made a Y-bar low' read inclusively (the bar's low is the lowest of the Y bars ending at it), HighestHighBreakout's '=' convention. Reaches back X - 1 + Y - 1.

candidates.name: UpperBandTouchHigherHigh
candidates.quote: Compare last two touches of the upper bollinger band. If those make a higher high, go long.
candidates.description: The current touch of the upper Bollinger band (high >= band) makes a higher high than the previous touch episode: long, on the first bar of the current episode whose high exceeds the previous episode's high. Short mirrors on lower-band touches making a lower low.

complexity.reason: band series history and episode bookkeeping over a variable window

library_check.evidence: BollingerBandCross fires on a close crossing back over a band; no rule compares successive band touches. TRIAGE: a twist (Decision 5), previously backtested (Q1).

notes: Treating consecutive touch bars as one episode is a concretization; touch-bar-by-touch-bar is the other reading (open question).
bbUpper[i] is recomputed fresh per offset from price (BollingerBand is fresh per bar).

candidates.name: UpperBandTouchBarBreak
candidates.quote: After a touch of the upper bollinger band, go long on the next candle to close above the high of the touch candle. If lower band is touched, invalidate the long trade.
candidates.description: Take the most recent upper-band touch bar T in 1..L. Long on the first close above high[T] since T, provided no bar since T touched the lower band. Short mirrors.

complexity.reason: band history plus an armed-level scan

library_check.evidence: Not a band cross; closest structural relative is PriorHighBreakoutWithOffset-style 'close above a prior bar's high', here anchored to the band-touch bar. Previously backtested (Q1).

notes: The expiry L is not in the note (default 10). A bar touching both bands on bar 0 does not fire.

candidates.name: BollingerWidthBelowAverage
candidates.quote: Filter is that range from upper to lower bollinger band is less than its average over the last X bars.
candidates.description: Bollinger band width (upper - lower = 2k x StdDev) below its own X-bar average: a low-volatility filter. k cancels, so it is StdDev(close, N) below its X-bar average.
candidates.pseudocode:
sd = stddev(close, N);   // a variable; its history is zero-filled before the first bar
pass = el_lt(sd, average(sd, X));

complexity.reason: average over a variable's own history (the BarRangeAboveStd mirror shape)

library_check.evidence: AtrAboveAverage (negated) is the same shape on ATR; nothing tests the StdDev of close against its own average. Width in price units, compared with itself, so the shift test passes.

notes: Zero-filled warm-up makes the average small early on, so the filter rarely passes during warm-up (the AtrAboveAverage note in reverse).

candidates.name: MaDistanceRegime
candidates.quote: Average distance between price and the moving average. Long term one is large in magnitude, short term one is small in magnitude. Enter long (v1) or short (v2) if the long term one is positive
candidates.description: Mean of (close - EMA) over a long window, in ATR units, is at least +A while the mean over a short window is within +/-B: price has lived well above the average but has come back to it. Long (v1); v2 is the flip. Short mirrors on a negative long-window mean.
candidates.sides: mirrored (the short-window band is identical on both sides)

library_check.evidence: CloseWithinAtrOfEma tests the current close's distance; no rule averages the distance over a window, let alone two.

notes: One MA and two averaging windows (TRIAGE's reading); MA type and length are not in the note (EMA 50).
close - ema is a variable: its history before the first evaluated bar is zero-filled in EL (EMA = 0 there), so longWindow must be warm before use.

candidates.name: TwoLargeBullBarsLittleOverlap
candidates.quote: Two large (>1 ATR) green candles with little overlap in the range
candidates.description: The last two bars are both up-close bars with range at least K x ATR, and their ranges overlap by at most F of the smaller range. Long; short mirrors on red bars.

library_check.evidence: LargeTrendBarCountInWindow(lookback 2, minCount 2, bodyFraction 0, largeMultiple K) AND ConsecutiveBarsLittleOverlap(consecutiveBars 1, maxOverlapFraction F) in two placements fire on the same bars (both use the current ATR and the smaller-range divisor). SpikeTrendBarsLowOverlap is the tick-overlap variant.

notes: 'Two' read as consecutive. Overlap measured against the smaller range (ConsecutiveBarsLittleOverlap's divisor); the note gives no divisor.

candidates.name: MaWickTouchesHoldSide
candidates.quote: The last X time price touched the moving average it was a wick and closed all on the same side of the average.
candidates.description: Each of the last X bars that touched the EMA did so with a wick only, the whole body staying above it (long: the average is holding as support); short mirrors with bodies below. A touch whose body straddles or closes on the other side resets the count.

library_check.evidence: EmaTouchRecovery is one bar trading through the EMA and closing back above; TwentyGapBarPullbackEntry counts bars between touches. Nothing counts consecutive wick-only touches.

notes: Pane 2 because the note states a condition with no entry; it can sit under any pullback entry.
MA type/length not in the note (EMA 50).

candidates.name: QuietBodiesBeforeBar
candidates.quote: Last ~10 bars have a small average body to range ratio.
candidates.description: Over the N bars ENDING ONE BAR AGO, the mean body is below F x the mean range (indecisive bars before the signal bar).
candidates.pseudocode:
for (i = lag; i < lag + N; ++i) { sb += absvalue(close[i] - open[i]); sr += high[i] - low[i]; }
pass = el_lt(sb / N, F * (sr / N));

library_check.evidence: AvgBodyBelowRangeFraction is this test current-bar-inclusive; adding a lag input (default 0 keeps it unchanged) gives the 'before the signal bar' window. If 'average body to range ratio' means the mean of per-bar ratios, it is AverageTailFractionBelow negated at 1 - F instead (see ON-76-b).

notes: Ratio of means chosen; mean of ratios is the other reading.

candidates.name: LargeStrongBarDirection
candidates.quote: Next bar is large (>1 ATR) with body >50% the range. Enter in direction of that bar.
candidates.description: The bar is an up-close bar with range at least K x ATR and body at least F of its range: long; mirrored on a down bar.
candidates.pseudocode: long = el_gt(close[0], open[0]) && el_ge(close[0] - open[0], 0.5 * (high[0] - low[0])) && el_ge(high[0] - low[0], 1.0 * atr);

library_check.evidence: ClimaxBar at climaxMultiple 1 (default 2), bodyFraction 0.5 (default 0.6) is this test; the note's strict '>' differs only on exact ties.

candidates.name: EmaSlopeAtrPerBar
candidates.quote: Use slope of ema as an indicator. Units are ATR/bar. ATR lookback same length as lookback over which you calculate the slope.
candidates.description: The EMA's rise over N bars, divided by N x ATR(N), is at least s ATR per bar (uptrend); short mirrored.
candidates.pseudocode: long = el_ge(ema - ema[N], s * N * atr(N));

library_check.evidence: EmaSlope fires when ema - ema[N] >= slopeAtr x ATR; with atrLookback = slopeLookback = N and slopeAtr = s x N it is this rule. A regression slope (the dropped R^2 sub-question hints at a fit) would be a different rule.

notes: The R^2 sub-question is dropped per TRIAGE.

candidates.name: GreenBarFraction
candidates.quote: Fraction of last X bars that closed green
candidates.description: At least a fraction F of the last X bars closed above their open (long); short mirrors on red.
candidates.pseudocode:
cnt = CountIF(close > open, X);
long = el_ge(cnt, fraction * X);

library_check.evidence: StrongBodyBarCountInWindow at strongBodyFraction = 0 counts exactly the up-close bars (close > open and body >= 0); minCount = F x windowBars. OppositeBodyCountInWindow is the same count read from the other colour against a maximum.

candidates.name: MeanBodyFraction
candidates.quote: Over last X bars, what is the average candle body as a fraction of the candle range
candidates.description: The mean over X bars of the per-bar body/range ratio is at least T (decisive bars); negate for indecisive.
candidates.pseudocode:
bf = average(absvalue(close - open) / (high - low + eps), X);
pass = el_ge(bf, T);

complexity.reason: window mean of a per-bar ratio

library_check.evidence: Body fraction = 1 - tail fraction per bar (both over range + eps), so mean body fraction >= T is AverageTailFractionBelow at maxTailFraction = 1 - T; equal up to the eps/(range+eps) term, which moves only near-zero-range bars.

notes: The ratio-of-means form is AvgBodyBelowRangeFraction (see ON-72-a and P3).

candidates.name: DowntrendCloseBelowEma
candidates.quote: Price trending down.
candidates.description: Trend context for ON-80-b: close below the EMA(N) for the short; above for the long.
candidates.pseudocode: long = el_gt(close[0], ema);   // short: el_lt(close[0], ema)

library_check.evidence: MINING's prescribed concretization of 'downtrend' is CloseBeyondEma at marginAtr 0.

candidates.name: IsolatedWickExtremeBreak
candidates.quote: At the extreme of the trend (X-bar low) there is a wick with at least Y*ATR of it having no bars in the close In the prior Z bars or Z bars since). Enter short on the first close below the wick.
candidates.description: A bar w makes the X-bar low, and the price band [low[w], low[w] + Y x ATR] is entered by no bar in the Z bars before w nor the Z bars after w (so it is confirmed Z bars late). After confirmation, short on the first close below low[w]. Long mirrors at an X-bar high with an isolated upper wick, entering on the first close above it.

complexity.reason: extreme detection with a two-sided isolation test, confirmed late, then an armed first-close trigger

library_check.evidence: SwingHigh's strength-Z pivot is the shape (an extreme with Z bars either side) but tests only that neighbours do not exceed the extreme, not that they stay Y x ATR away; NotableBarExtremeLevel arms a level from a strong bar, not an isolated wick.

notes: Reading per TRIAGE (Brian 2026-11-05). atrAt(w) is the ATR as of bar w, which needs an ATR history buffer.
maxWaitBars (how long the level stays armed after confirmation) is not in the note; see open_questions.

candidates.name: EmaTouchAfterLongAbsence
candidates.quote: Look at long-term ema (~200 bar) and see how many bars there are between touches. When the most recent time between touches is much longer than recent ones, enter is such a direction that you are expecting the trend line not to hold.
candidates.description: The bar touches the 200 EMA (range contains it) and the gap since the previous touch is at least K x the mean of the N gaps before that. Enter in the direction of the crossing: long when the bar before the touch was entirely below the EMA (price coming up through it), short when entirely above.

complexity.reason: persistent touch-gap history and an EMA

library_check.evidence: TwentyGapBarPullbackEntry fires on the first touch after a FIXED gap count and buys the HOLD (close stays above); this uses an adaptive threshold (K x recent mean gap) and trades THROUGH the average, the opposite direction. EmaGapBarRun counts the gap but has no direction or adaptivity.

notes: Gap history lives in a fixed ring of N + 1 slots updated on touch bars.

candidates.name: EmaNoTouchWindow
candidates.quote: When ema has not touched within the last X bars. Pair this with volatility filter. Test both directions.
candidates.description: No bar's range has touched the 200 EMA in the last X bars; direction-agnostic. A volatility filter (e.g. ON-57-a) goes in its own placement.
candidates.pseudocode: pass = gapRun >= X;   // persistent counter reset on a touching bar

library_check.evidence: EmaGapBarRun at emaLength 200 (default 20) and gapBarsRequired X; 'test both directions' is EmaGapBar or a flip in another placement.

candidates.name: RangeOutsidePriorRangeFraction
candidates.quote: Generalized, which fraction of the bars range lies outside the range of the previous X bars?
candidates.description: The part of the bar's high-low range lying above the prior X-bar high or below the prior X-bar low, as a fraction of the bar's range, is at least T: a trend bar. Negate for a consolidation bar.

library_check.evidence: BreakoutClearsPriorExtremeByMargin and CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh test that the bar clears the prior window extreme by a fixed margin; InsideBar (T = 0, negated, X = 1) and OutsideBar are the degenerate ends. None measures the fraction of the bar outside the prior range.

notes: Direction-agnostic as TRIAGE describes it; a directional variant would count only the side beyond the prior high.
MaxList here selects between a price difference and 0, outside EL_FEATURES's accepted scope (tick-grid price operands); a plain if/else in the twin avoids it.
The note's ATR/indicators-book normalization is not used (TRIAGE).

candidates.name: SwingLowSupportZone

library_check.evidence: LevelTouchCount counts bar touches of one level; DoubleExtremePullback builds a level from two pivots within matchTicks. Neither clusters M pivots with a dispersion test.

candidates.name: CloseAtSupportZone

candidates.description: A valid I2 support zone exists and the bar's low has come into it (low <= zoneHi + tol x ATR) while the close stays at or above its bottom: price is at support. Short mirrors at a resistance zone.

candidates.name: SwingStructureTrend

candidates.pseudocode: long = haveHi2 && haveLo2 && el_gt(hi1, hi2) && el_gt(lo1, lo2);

library_check.evidence: HigherSwingLow (long: higher swing low; short: lower swing high) is one series per side; I4 needs both series agreeing. candidates.name: AtrToRangeCongestion
candidates.quote: Indicator: ATRX / (X_Bar_High - X_Bar_Low) Maybe it measures congestion zones?
candidates.description: ATR(X) / (X-bar high - X-bar low) at least T: congestion. Equivalent to RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple with rangeLookback = atrLookback = X and rangeAtrMultiple = 1/T. candidates.name: BodyMaBandBreakout
candidates.quote: Fit a moving average to the higher end of the bodies (open of red bar / close of green bar) and another to the lower end. Go long when price is more than X*(high ma low ma) above the (moving?) average of the

library_check.evidence: Keltner/Bollinger bands are a centre plus a multiple of ATR/StdDev; this band's width is the mean body extent, and the test is a level, not a cross. CloseBeyondEma is the single-MA analogue.

candidates.name: BodyToWickRatio
candidates.quote: Ratio of average body size to average wick length as an indicator. Use where you would use a volatility indicator.
candidates.description: Mean body / mean wick over N bars below T (wick-dominated); negate for body-dominated. Since mean wick = mean range - mean body, body/wick < T <=> mean body < T/(1+T) x mean range.
candidates.pseudocode:
avgBody = average(absvalue(close - open), N); avgRange = average(high - low, N);
pass = el_lt(avgBody, (T / (1 + T)) * avgRange);

library_check.evidence: AvgBodyBelowRangeFraction (ratio of the two window means, current-inclusive) at weakBodyFraction = T/(1+T): T = 0.67 is the library default 0.4. Exact algebra, not an approximation, with wick = upper + lower tail = range - body.

candidates.name: BreakoutDirectionShare

candidates.name: MaSideFlipRun

candidates.name: FractalMovePullbackContraction

candidates.name: BreakawayPullbackBreak

open_questions.question: A bar that is both a swing high and a swing low (an outside-bar pivot) enters the pivot sequence twice at the same bar. Which goes first for the fractal-order rules (#50, #51, #53, #59), or should such a bar be dropped from the sequence?
Fire on the bar the pattern completes (event, specced) or on every bar until the next pivot changes the pattern (state)? It matters with stop-and-reverse exits.
#50's box is stated only as low, high, low, high. Should the mirror ordering (high, low, high, low, also contracting) qualify too, as Brian ruled for the #1-3 channels?
Coefficient of variation of which series? CV of close is std/mean of price and fails the shift test; specced on true range. Bar range or close-to-close changes are the alternatives.
Is a 'touch' each bar at or above the upper band, or one episode per run of consecutive touching bars (specced)? Bar-by-bar fires on most bars of a strong rally.

Under TRIAGE's wording P8 is P4 at F = 1 (same bars). What makes them distinct: does P4 count breakouts within a fixed bar window rather than the last Y events, or do they differ in what counts as a breakout (high/low vs close)?

How is the breakaway move delimited? Specced as the run of consecutive up-close bars ending at the move's high, with the pullback after it; alternatives are the lowest low before the high or a fixed window.

Which swing lows form a zone: the M most recent consecutive ones (specced), or any M of the last P that fit the spread test? And what pane-2 condition should the zone feed: price at support (specced as I2-b) or price inside it?
How long does a confirmed isolated wick stay armed for the 'first close below'? Specced with maxWaitBars = 30.
'Fractal low length ~3': strength 3 (specced, per the MINING convention) or a 3-bar fractal (strength 1)?

summary: Brian's KEEP ideas from Strategies.pdf rows #50-#85, Indicators I1-I5, phone notes P2-P16 and the P1 visit family. Fractal-order rules (#50, #51, #53, #59, P6) share the ON-50-a pivot-sequence primitive built on the measured SwingHigh/SwingLow port; one-sided pivot rules (#52, #58, P9, P13, P15, I2-I4) read the per-side occurrences. Several filters resolve to existing Brooks rules by algebra (I5 and the Choppiness Index to RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple, P3 to AvgBodyBelowRangeFraction, #76a/b to StrongBodyBarCountInWindow / AverageTailFractionBelow, #73 to EmaSlope).

resolutions.answer: HIGH candle = CLOSE above the 50-bar high (symmetric with LOW). Every bar between the two L's (H's) must be a C candle.
Level = a cluster of wick lows within a tolerance, built like the I2 support zone (not the most recent swing low).

Zone: scanning back N bars, the K+ most recent 1-bar swing lows all within X*ATR of each other, with std dev of those lows <= k*ATR; bottom = lowest of them; a close more than 0.5*ATR below the bottom kills it. #26 needs two distinct stacked zones. No pane-2 'near zone' condition for now.
A bar that is both a swing high and a swing low counts as both, ordered by bar direction: a green bar (close > open) is low-then-high, a red bar high-then-low.
The mirror order (high, low, high, low with the last two inside the first two) also counts.
Breakaway move = a run of consecutive bull bars each with range >= k*ATR; measured from the first run bar's open to the run's highest high.
Cancel the armed setup if a later bar trades back into the band. Add a window input W, counted from the wick bar, constrained W > Z.
'Fractal low length ~3' = swing strength 3 (three bars each side); the pullback must be at least 3 bars.
